quote: Territory mismatch. The exclusive distribution right covers only four states (DE, MD, NJ, PA) under Distribution Agreement § 1.12, but the non-compete covers six states (adding NY and VA) under Side Letter § 1.1. Harrow Creek is restricted from competing in New York and Virginia without receiving any exclusive distribution rights there. ... Consider whether to request a modification of the Side Letter ... (e.g., narrowing the Territory to match the Distribution Agreement's four-state territory ...)
reason: The memo identifies the core problem. The Side Letter's expanded Territory adds NY and VA, so the non-compete covers six states while exclusivity under DA § 1.12 covers four. It notes the 18-month post-term tail and recommends conforming the Territory to the four-state definition. One gap: it does not explicitly tie the Territory override to DA § 19.4. It cites § 19.4 only in Issue 6 (governing law), where it notes the Side Letter ranks above the Agreement body. However, it treats the six-state Side Letter definition as controlling the non-compete, which is the substance of the issue.
